text:
A: Hiya! Oh, can you hear me alright?
B: Yeah, I can hear you. Hiya. Sorry, I've only just sat down, I've come straight in from work.
A: Oh no, you're fine. I'm Gemma. I'm in Beeston, near Nottingham.
B: Kerry. I'm down in Bridgwater, Somerset.
A: Oh lovely. Have you been on shift today then?
B: Yeah, I work on the tills at the big supermarket on the edge of town, and the customer service desk. To be honest, today was a nightmare. I had a woman kick off at me over a ten pence coupon. Ten pence! She wanted the manager and everything, and I'm stood there thinking, love, I'll give you ten pence out me own purse if you'll just go away.
A: Oh, I know that sort of person. We get parents like that at parents' evening.
B: Are you a teacher then? I thought you might be, with the lanyard and that.
A: Yeah, I'm Head of Maths at a secondary in Nottingham. Sorry, it's still on, isn't it? I never take it off.
B: Maths. God. I got a D in maths, I'll tell you that now so you don't ask.
A: Ha, no, I wasn't going to ask! Honestly, half the kids I teach think they can't do it, and it's mostly that nobody's sort of explained it properly. Did you do alright on that puzzle thing at the start?
B: No. I didn't see the point of it, to be honest. I just clicked on stuff till it went away.
A: Yeah, no, I was the same, and I'm meant to be good at that kind of thing! I kept second-guessing myself.
B: Well that makes me feel better then.
A: Have you got kids yourself?
B: One. Callum, he's seventeen. He's doing mechanics at college. He eats everything in the fridge, I'm not even joking. I do a big shop and it's gone by Wednesday.
A: Oh, don't. My Josh is twelve and he only eats beige food. Chicken nuggets, chips, a plain cob, that's it. And my daughter's fifteen, so we've got the moods as well.
B: A cob?
A: A bread roll. Sorry, is that just us round here?
B: I've never heard that in my life. A cob. That's what my nan used to call a horse.
A: Oh, that's brilliant. No, it's a roll, I promise. What do you do for your tea then, after a shift like that?
B: Dinner, you mean. Probably sausage and mash. I picked up some reduced sausages on the way out, yellow sticker, forty pence.
A: Ooh, bargain. And yeah, sorry, dinner, tea, whatever. I've just put a spag bol on. Friday's a chippy tea though, that's non-negotiable in our house.
B: Same. There's a chip shop by my mum's that's proper. My mum's round mine most days anyway, she lives ten minutes off.
A: Mine's ten minutes away too! She does the school pick-ups for me. I don't know what I'd do without her, honestly, with the hours I do.
B: Are the hours bad then? I always thought teachers finished at three.
A: Ha, everyone thinks that. No, it's more like fifty-odd hours with the marking. There's a pile of books behind me I've not touched yet. Is that the kind of thing, sorry, I'm rambling...
B: No, you're alright. I couldn't do it. I'd lose my rag with the kids.
A: You'd be surprised, you get used to it. The photocopier's what makes me lose my rag, that always jams on deadline day.
